sentences.Jeg er norsk og har bodd i Mosambik en g: I'm Norwegian and have lived in Mozambique for quite a while.
sentences.Der har jeg truffet verdens kjekkeste ma: There I've met the most handsome man in the world!
sentences.Nå må jeg dra hjem igjen, men vi er fore: Now I have to go home again, but we're in love and want to live together in Norway.
sentences.Jeg vet at kjæresten min må ha oppholdst: I know my boyfriend has to have a residence permit, and that it's hard to get.
sentences.Hva skal vi gjøre for å få dette til?: What should we do to make this happen?
sentences.Har noen vært i en liknende situasjon?: Has anyone been in a similar situation?
sentences.Jeg kan kanskje gi deg et råd, men bare: Maybe I can give you some advice, but only if you're planning to get married.
sentences.Da kan han søke om noe som heter forlove: Then he can apply for something called a fiancé permit in Mozambique (you can read more about it on UDI's website).
sentences.Med en slik tillatelse kan kjæresten din: With a permit like that your boyfriend can travel to Norway and stay here for six months, but during that time you have to get married.
sentences.Og hvis vi ikke gifter oss?: And if we don't get married?
Then he has to leave the country.
sentences.Seks måneder er altfor kort tid, synes j: Six months is far too short, I think.
In Norway he will face many challenges.
sentences.Hvordan vet vi at han vil trives - etter: How do we know he'll be happy here - after such a short time?
sentences.Enig! Et halvt år er kort tid, men slik: Agreed! Six months is a short time, but those are the rules.
You have to think it over carefully.
sentences.Er det noen som har erfaringer her?: Does anyone here have any experience of this?
sentences.Jeg vil høre om alt, både positive og ne: I want to hear about everything, both positive and negative experiences.
